$comment: Shared Go/TypeScript case table for results[].rawSourceRecord (ADR-0017 §5). Both shipped validators read this file, because the closure is written with additionalProperties: the Go validator is a draft-07 engine that silently ignores unevaluatedProperties, so a closure written the house way would hold in TypeScript alone and the bounded field would be bounded in one language only. Each case is injected as the rawSourceRecord of the document's single result.

cases.name: a utf-8 JSON record
cases.why: the three required members are the whole contract

cases.name: a record located by pointer
cases.why: pointer is the optional fourth member

cases.name: an XML record inside a JSON document
cases.why: mediaType describes the record, not the document carrying it

cases.name: a base64 record
cases.why: bytes that are not valid UTF-8 text carry as base64

cases.name: an empty content string
cases.why: no minLength is imposed: an empty record is a producer question, not a schema one

cases.name: no content
cases.why: content is required — a record with no bytes carries nothing

cases.name: no encoding
cases.why: encoding is required: bytes a consumer has to guess how to read are not carriage

cases.name: no mediaType
cases.why: mediaType is required, the same rule §2 sets for an embedding artifact

cases.name: an undeclared member
cases.why: the field is CLOSED — this is the case the Go validator would miss under unevaluatedProperties, and the reason the closure uses additionalProperties

cases.name: an encoding outside the enum
cases.why: utf-8 and base64 are the only encodings, matching §3's artifact pair

cases.name: a string instead of an object
cases.why: the record is an object with declared members, never a bare blob

cases.name: a non-string content
cases.why: content is the record's bytes as a string; a parsed object belongs in the artifact's document member, not here
